Synthetic fixtures generated by `python3 generate.py`, with no customer content.
Word 16.113.2 exported all four DOCX files to PDF on 2026-09-29 using the
pagination tooling's lock-aware `word_export.py`. `word_lines.py` supplied
the marker baselines and page boundaries recorded in `word.json`.

Each table has three columns. The first two cells span the first three rows
and contain eight and ten paragraphs, each with an exact 12 pt line height.
The third column labels those rows `H001` through `H003`. Both vertical
merges therefore need growth beyond the rows' natural total of 36 pt.
The reversed fixtures exchange the first two columns.

All cells have zero margins and no borders; all rows disallow splitting.
Pages are 360 by 450 pt with 36 pt margins. Body rows are 12 pt tall and
carry `B001` onward in the third column. `END` follows the table.

| Fixtures | Word pages | Body rows by page | Repeated header rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `same-span`, `same-span-reversed` | 1 | 1–20 | None |
| `repeated-header`, `repeated-header-reversed` | 3 | 1–21; 22–42; 43–60 | First three rows on pages 2 and 3 |

In every export, `H001`, `H002`, `H003`, and the first body row have baselines
at 45.5, 57.5, 69.5, and 165.6 pt. Their differences give merged row heights
of 12.0, 12.0, and 96.1 pt. Tests allow 0.3 pt for PDF baseline rounding.
The repeated headers have the same baselines on all three pages.

`rowStart` and `rowEnd` in `word.json` are zero-based, exclusive-end source
row windows. The first three source rows precede `B001`; repeated copies
are represented separately by `repeatedHeaderRows`.
